summary: Alleghany County lookout tower built by the Conservation Corps in 1935; NGS notes say it was torn down and removed by 1991, and a planned move to Green Mountain is unconfirmed.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
facts.design: 59-foot 3-inch steel tower with a one-room ground cabin
facts.status_note: Torn down and removed, per an NCGS 1991 recovery note; no source confirms where it went

events.note: Conservation Corps erected a 59-foot 3-inch steel tower with a one-room ground cabin at a cost of $963.05, funded through the Emergency Conservation Works program
A temporary woman lookout died after a fall down the tower steps, per a Statesville Daily Record report quoted by Forest Lookouts
NCGS recovery note: the fire tower was to be removed within a year and erected on Green Mountain about 6 miles northwest; the move is not confirmed in sources read
NCGS recovery note: the lookout tower had been torn down and removed

notes_for_editor: Build year, design, cost and the 1952 death come from the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes a state biennial report and a newspaper; no primary report was read. The 1952 date (April 23, 1952) and the Statesville Daily Record attribution are on that page. Height is converted by hand from 59 ft 3 in to 18.06 m. The link from the tower to FZ1901 rests on tnlandforms and on the NGS datasheet's own reference to the lookout tower. The FZ1903 listing has two lines (codes XX and NN); the story cites only the XX line. The 1970 move to Green Mountain is unconfirmed; a check of Green Mountain lookout records would settle it. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the station-in-woods description is in the 1970 NCGS note, not 1991, and the 2002 recovery has its own note. The 1970 note calls the clearing 'the former site' of the tower in the same note that says the tower is still to be removed, so that wording is kept as the source's. The brief's registers field lists NGS, a survey registry rather than a lookout register; left unchanged.
